subproblem.title: First-variation control of a scaled restricted measure gives locally bounded first variation and a bound on ‖δW‖
subproblem.statement: Let Ω ⊆ ℝ^N, μ a measure on ℝ^N × G(N,n), W an n-varifold on Ω, and c, β ∈ [0,∞] with c ≠ ∞ and β ≠ ∞, such that W.measure = c • μ⌞(Ω × G(N,n)). Assume that for every C¹ field X : ℝ^N → ℝ^N with compact support, tsupport X ⊆ Ω and ‖X(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y, we have ofReal|∫ div_S X(z) dμ(z,S)| ≤ β, where div_S X(z) = Varifold.tangentialDivergence X z S. Then W has locally bounded first variation, and variationMeasure W O ≤ c·β for every O with IsRelCompactOpenIn O Ω.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (Ω : Set (Euclidean N)) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n)) (W : Varifold N n Ω) (c β : ℝ≥0∞), c ≠ ∞ → β ≠ ∞ → W.measure = c • μ.restrict (Ω ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) → (∀ X : Euclidean N → Euclidean N, ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ Ω → (∀ y, ‖X y‖ ≤ 1) → ENNReal.ofReal |∫ z, Varifold.tangentialDivergence X z.1 z.2 ∂μ| ≤ β) → W.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation ∧ ∀ O : Set (Euclidean N), IsRelCompactOpenIn O Ω → variationMeasure W O ≤ c * β
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof. That step proves the identity δW_j(X) = τ⁻¹∫div_S X dV_j and passes from a bound on |δW_j(X)| to firstVariationNormOn, LBFV and variationMeasure. Here the rescaled-divergence estimate is abstracted as the hypothesis.

Notation: δW(X) = W.firstVariation X = ∫ div_S X(z) dW.measure(z,S).

1. (First-variation identity.) Let X ∈ Varifold.TestVectorField Ω: C¹, compact support, tsupport X ⊆ Ω. We claim δW(X) = c.toReal·∫ div_S X dμ.
  - By W.measure = c • μ.restrict(Ω × G) and integral_smul_measure (∫ f d(c•m) = c.toReal • ∫ f dm, for every f and c), δW(X) = c.toReal·∫_{Ω×G} div_S X dμ.
  - Let (z,S) ∉ Ω × G. Then z ∉ Ω, so z ∉ tsupport X. By Varifold.support_tangentialDivergence_subset, the support of (z,S) ↦ div_S X(z) lies in tsupport X × G, so div_S X(z) = 0.
  - Hence ∫_{Ω×G} div_S X dμ = ∫ div_S X dμ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero), proving the claim.

2. (Uniform bound.) For every set O ⊆ ℝ^N, W.firstVariationNormOn O ≤ c·β. By definition, firstVariationNormOn O is the supremum over X ∈ TestVectorField Ω of: ofReal|δW(X)| if X.UnitSupportedIn O (tsupport X ⊆ O and ‖X(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y), and 0 otherwise. By iSup_le it suffices to bound each term.
  - The term 0 is ≤ c·β.
  - If X is unit-supported in O: by step 1 and c.toReal ≥ 0, |δW(X)| = c.toReal·|∫ div_S X dμ| (abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg). Hence ofReal|δW(X)| = ofReal(c.toReal)·ofReal|∫ div_S X dμ| = c·ofReal|∫ div_S X dμ| (ENNReal.ofReal_mul; ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, using c ≠ ∞).
  - This is ≤ c·β by the hypothesis applied to X: X is C¹ with compact support, tsupport X ⊆ Ω because X is a test field on Ω, and ‖X(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y.

3. (Locally bounded first variation.) c·β ≠ ∞ because c ≠ ∞ and β ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.mul_ne_top). By step 2, for every open O with compact closure contained in Ω, W.firstVariationNormOn O ≤ c·β < ∞. This is W.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation (call it hLBFV).

4. (Bound for ‖δW‖.) Let IsRelCompactOpenIn O Ω: O open, closure O compact, closure O ⊆ Ω.
  - By definition of variationMeasure, and since W has LBFV (positive branch of the dite, dif_pos), variationMeasure W = W.firstVariationRieszMeasure hLBFV.
  - SimonGMT Varifold.firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm, applicable because O is open with compact closure ⊆ Ω, gives W.firstVariationRieszMeasure hLBFV O = W.firstVariationNormOn O.
  - By step 2 this is ≤ c·β, so variationMeasure W O ≤ c·β. ∎
proof_key_steps: For test fields X on Ω, δW(X) = c.toReal·∫ div_S X dμ (integral_smul_measure; the integrand vanishes off Ω × G by support_tangentialDivergence_subset).
Hence ofReal|δW(X)| = c·ofReal|∫ div_S X dμ| ≤ c·β for unit fields, so firstVariationNormOn O ≤ c·β for every O (iSup_le).
variationMeasure W = firstVariationRieszMeasure (dif_pos), and firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm gives variationMeasure W O ≤ c·β when IsRelCompactOpenIn O Ω.

audit.reason: The proof removes the restriction using vanishing tangential divergence outside the test-field support, then scales the integral and bounds the defining supremum. Finiteness gives LBFV, and the pinned Riesz-measure identity gives the stated variation bound. The cited integral identities require no omitted integrability assumption.
